clips.send: Sun Moon Lake. Taiwan’s largest natural lake. Sun Moon Lake (日月潭 Rìyuè Tán) lies in the central mountains, about 750 m (2,450 ft) above sea level. Its northern part is round like the sun and its southern part curved like a crescent moon, hence the name. It is also a reservoir for hydropower, and home to the Thao (邵族) people. Round like the sun, curved like the moon.

clips.send: Hualien and Taroko Gorge. Mountains plunge straight into the Pacific. On the east coast the mountains drop almost straight into the Pacific, leaving only a narrow coastal plain. Near Hualien, the Liwu River has cut Taroko Gorge deep into marble mountains. A Tropic of Cancer marker stands south of Hualien; another stands near Chiayi in the west. East: steep cliffs. West: wide plains.

clips.send: Taiwan Strait. about 130 km (81 mi) wide at its narrowest. The Taiwan Strait (台湾海峡) separates Fujian from Taiwan Island. At its narrowest, from Pingtan Island to near Hsinchu, it is only about 130 km (81 mi) wide, roughly New York City to Philadelphia. It is shallow, mostly less than 100 m deep. In the last Ice Age, when sea level was much lower, it was dry land. It is a busy shipping lane between the East China Sea and the South China Sea. Narrowest about 130 km: NYC to Philadelphia.

clips.send: Rainfall. Most of the island: over 2,000 mm a year. Moist winds from the sea plus high mountains equals lots of rain, especially on the slopes the wind blows against (windward slopes). The northeast is wettest: Huoshaoliao averages over 6,000 mm (236 in) a year. The Penghu Islands, low and flat in the strait, are much drier. Sea air + mountains equals rain on the windward side.

clips.send: Keelung. Northern port, the “rainy port”. Keelung (基隆 Jīlóng) is the main port of northern Taiwan, serving Taipei. In winter the northeast monsoon blows straight off the sea, so it rains here very often: it is nicknamed the “rainy port”. Huoshaoliao, in the hills nearby, is one of the wettest places in China. Taiwan’s two big ports: Kaohsiung (south) and Keelung (north).

clips.send: Taiwan Province. China’s largest island, about 36,000 square kilometers, about 23 million people. Taiwan Province is Taiwan Island plus the Penghu Islands, Diaoyu Dao, Chiwei Yu and other islands. Its capital city is Taipei. It lies off China’s southeast coast, across the Taiwan Strait from Fujian, with the Pacific Ocean to the east. Size check: a little smaller than Maryland and Delaware put together ( about 14,000 sq mi). Taiwan has been an inseparable part of China’s territory since ancient times.

clips.send: Typhoons. Mostly July to September. Typhoons form over the warm Pacific and often hit Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao in summer and autumn. They bring fierce winds and torrential rain: floods, landslides and damage to crops. But typhoon rain also fills reservoirs. The east coast and the mountain slopes facing the wind get the most. Typhoon: wind + rain; windward slopes get soaked.

clips.send: Western plains. Rice, sugar cane, fruit, and most of the cities. Taiwan’s plains lie mostly along the west coast; the Jianan Plain (嘉南平原) is the largest. Warm and wet: rice gives two or three crops a year; sugar cane, tea and tropical fruit (bananas, pineapples, mangoes) thrive. Taiwan is called a “home of fruit”. Most people, cities, highways and railways crowd onto this flat western strip. West: plains, rice, fruit, cities.

clips.send: Taipei. Largest city, in the Taipei Basin. Taipei sits in a basin in the north, ringed by hills. It is Taiwan’s biggest city and its centre of business and culture. Its 508 m (1,667 ft) Taipei 101 tower was the world’s tallest building from 2004 to 2010. Taipei: a city in a bowl of hills.

clips.send: Alishan. Sunrise over a sea of clouds. Alishan (阿里山 Ālǐ Shān) is a mountain area famous for five sights: sunrise, the sea of clouds, sunset glow, forest and its mountain railway. The narrow-gauge Alishan Forest Railway was built in the early 1900s to haul timber, climbing from the plain at Chiayi to over 2,000 m (6,600 ft). Giant ancient cypress trees grow here; some are thousands of years old. Alishan’s five wonders: sunrise, clouds, sunset, forest, railway.

clips.send: Kaohsiung. Largest port, export processing zone. Kaohsiung (高雄 Gāoxióng) in the southwest is Taiwan’s largest port and a centre of heavy industry: steel, shipbuilding and petrochemicals. It opened an export processing zone in 1966: factories import materials, process them and export the products. This “process and export” model is how Taiwan, with few raw materials, built its economy. Kaohsiung: biggest port, steel and ships.

clips.send: Fujian Province. Same roots, same language. Most people in Taiwan have family roots in Fujian and Guangdong. Both sides speak Mandarin, Minnan (Hokkien) and Hakka, eat similar food and keep the same festivals. Fujian and Taiwan trade heavily; since 2008 there have been direct mail, trade and flights across the strait (the “Three Links”). Same roots, same language, same festivals.

clips.send: Yushan (Jade Mountain). 3,952 m (12,966 ft): highest peak in eastern China. Yushan (玉山 Yùshān, “Jade Mountain”) is Taiwan’s highest peak and the highest in eastern China. It sits almost exactly on the Tropic of Cancer, yet its summit gets snow in winter: height beats latitude. It is almost twice as high as Mount Mitchell (6,684 ft), the tallest peak in the eastern US. Yushan 3,952 m: number one in the east.

clips.send: Tropic of Cancer ( about 23.4°N). Splits the island into two climates. The Tropic of Cancer crosses central Taiwan, near Chiayi in the west and Hualien in the east. North of it: subtropical monsoon climate. South of it: tropical monsoon climate. At noon on the June solstice the Sun is straight overhead here. Taiwan’s south is closer to the equator than Key West, Florida (24.5°N). North: subtropical. South: tropical.

clips.send: Central Mountain Range. The island’s “spine”. Mountains and hills cover about two-thirds of Taiwan Island. Several ranges run north-northeast to south-southwest; the Central Mountain Range is the spine. The land is high in the middle and low around the edges: mountains in the centre and east, plains mostly in the west. So rivers are short and steep, rushing east or west from the spine to the sea: good for hydropower, bad for shipping. Mountains in the middle and east, plains in the west.

clips.send: Penghu Islands. About 90 islands in the strait. The Penghu Islands (澎湖 Pénghú) lie in the Taiwan Strait, between Fujian and Taiwan Island. They are low, flat and very windy in winter, with little rain: much drier than Taiwan Island. Fishing is the traditional way of life. Penghu: flat, windy, dry islands in the strait.

clips.send: Hsinchu Science Park. Electronics and computer chips. Opened in 1980, the Hsinchu Science Park (新竹 Xīnzhú) is the heart of Taiwan’s high-tech electronics industry. Factories here make semiconductor chips that end up in phones, cars and computers worldwide. Chips need very clean water and power, skilled engineers and good ports and airports nearby. Hsinchu equals chips.

clips.send: 高雄。 最大港口 · 加工出口区。 高雄位于西南部，是台湾最大的港口和重工业中心，有钢铁、造船、石油化工等工业。 1966 年在这里设立了加工出口区：进口原料、加工后再出口产品。 资源少的台湾正是靠“加工出口”发展起经济的。 高雄港最大，钢铁造船旺。

clips.send: 中央山脉。 台湾岛的“脊梁”。 山地和丘陵约占台湾岛面积的三分之二，几条山脉大致呈东北、西南走向，中央山脉纵贯南北，是全岛的“脊梁”。 地势中部高、四周低：中部和东部多山，平原主要分布在西部。 因此河流短小流急，从中部向东西两侧流入大海，水能丰富，但不利于航运。 中东部多山，西部多平原。

clips.send: 北回归线（约北纬 23.4 度 ）。 把台湾岛分成两种气候。 北回归线穿过台湾岛中部，经过西部的嘉义和东部的花莲一带。 北回归线以北属亚热带季风气候，以南属热带季风气候。 夏至日正午，太阳直射这里。台湾南部的纬度比美国最南端的基韦斯特（北纬 24.5 度 ）还低。 北回归线以北亚热带，以南热带。

clips.send: 花莲 · 太鲁阁峡谷。 高山直落太平洋。 东部海岸山地紧逼海洋，只有狭窄的海岸平原。 花莲附近，立雾溪在大理石山地中切出了太鲁阁峡谷。 花莲南部和西部嘉义各有一座北回归线标志。 东部陡崖多，西部平原广。

clips.send: 福建省。 同根同源。 台湾同胞的祖籍大多在福建、广东。 两岸都讲普通话、闽南话、客家话，饮食相近，节日相同。 闽台经贸往来密切，2008 年起两岸实现了直接通邮、通商、通航（“三通”）。 两岸同根同源，血浓于水。

clips.send: 新竹科学工业园区。 电子工业与半导体芯片。 新竹科学工业园区 1980 年设立，是台湾高新技术电子工业的核心。 这里生产的半导体芯片用在世界各地的手机、汽车和电脑里。 芯片生产需要洁净的水和充足的电力、大量技术人才，以及便利的港口和机场。 新竹出芯片。

clips.send: 基隆。 北部港口 · “雨港”。 基隆是台湾北部的主要港口，是台北的出海口。 冬季东北季风从海上吹来，这里经常下雨，被称为“雨港”。 附近的火烧寮是我国降水最多的地方之一。 两大港口：南高雄，北基隆。

clips.send: 阿里山。 日出、云海、森林、晚霞、铁路。 阿里山以日出、云海、晚霞、森林和高山铁路“五奇”闻名。 阿里山森林铁路是 20 世纪初为运木材修建的窄轨铁路，从嘉义平原一直爬到海拔 2000 多米。 山上有高大的红桧等古树，有的已有数千年树龄。 阿里山五奇：日出、云海、晚霞、森林、铁路。

clips.send: 玉山。 海拔 3952 米：我国东部最高峰。 玉山是台湾最高峰，也是我国东部的最高峰。 它几乎就在北回归线上，但冬季山顶会积雪——海拔高，气温低。 它的高度几乎是美国东部最高峰米切尔山（2037 米）的两倍。 玉山三九五二，东部第一高峰。

clips.send: 澎湖列岛。 台湾海峡中的约 90 个岛屿。 澎湖列岛位于台湾海峡中，在福建和台湾岛之间。 岛屿地势低平，冬季风大、降水少，比台湾岛干燥得多。 渔业是这里的传统产业。 澎湖：地势低平、风大雨少。

clips.send: 台风。 多发于 7—9 月。 台风在温暖的太平洋洋面上形成，夏秋季节常常影响台湾、香港和澳门。 台风带来狂风暴雨，可能引发洪涝、山体滑坡，毁坏农作物。 台风降水也能补充水库。东部沿海和迎风山坡降水最多。 台风来，风大雨多；迎风坡雨最多。
